content.introduction: Asian stocks hit record highs driven by a strong AI-led rally and robust corporate earnings, with Japan’s Nikkei index crossing the 62,000 mark for the first time after returning from a long holiday. South Korean and Taiwanese stocks also touched record highs. MSCI’s broad Asia-Pacific index outside Japan rose one percent, reaching another all-time high and gaining seven percent over the week. This surge was fueled by growing hopes of a possible peace deal in the Middle East, which also led to a slip in the US dollar and extended losses in oil prices.

[0:08] and oil prices extended recent losses, Japan's Nicay index crossed the 62,000 mark for the first time after returning from a long holiday driven by a strong
[0:17] AILE rally and robust corporate earnings. South Korean and Taiwanese stocks also touched record highs. MCI's

Palantir Technologies, a data analytics company closely tied to the US and Israeli defence sectors, was among the biggest gainers, with its shares soaring 29.5 percent on the back of forecast-busting second-quarter revenue of $1.94bn.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which tracks 30 blue-chip companies, set a new record for a second straight day, climbing 1.7 percent to 54,085.88.

The rally continued in Asia on Wednesday, with key indexes in Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong making gains. [...] Tokyo’s benchmark Nikkei 225 finished up 3.7 percent, while the Kospi in Seoul rose 3.8 percent.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index edged up 0.3 percent.

Brent crude, the primary international benchmark for oil prices, ticked up after falling about 5 percent overnight on hopes for a breakthrough on the Strait of Hormuz, which transported about one-fifth of global oil supplies before the start of the US-Israel war on Iran in late February. [...] The US military said on Tuesday that the strait was “free and open” to all commercial vessels despite Tehran’s repeated insistence that it has the right to control the movement of traffic in the waterway.

“Over the past three months, US forces have assisted more than 1,000 vessels in successfully transiting the strait despite unwarranted Iranian aggression, and these transits continue today,” US Central Command said in a post on social media.
